title: Pier Cap Cheek Wall Design
case_name: C018 - Pier Cap Cheek Wall Design (CAD walls and mats of 19 October 2026, C001 wind values)
sources_intro: The calculation starts from the pier cheek walls and their mats as the current CAD model holds them (decisions D-059 and D-061) and from the wind values of the superstructure wind calculation C001; every input names the model record, the journal module or the provision it comes from. Edit an input in Cell 2 to study a change.
intro: **What it does.** Designs the two solid cheek walls on the ends of the pier cap for wind acting directly on them: the LRFD 3.8.1.2.1 pressure with the C001 wind speed, exposure coefficient and gust factor and the substructure drag coefficient (Strength III, Strength V and Service I, WS = 1.0), the wind delivered to the pier per LRFD 3.8.1.2.3b, and the wall as a cantilever from the cap top: flexure and minimum reinforcement at the cap top and at the recessed panel, crack control and the SDG service stress limit, shear, interface shear at the construction joint, straight development of the verticals into the cap, shrinkage and temperature steel, spacing, cover and the SDM minimum thickness.

**Starting case.** The CAD walls (48 x 48 x 12 in, 3/4 in recessed panel) with their mats: one centred mat of six #4 verticals and six #4 horizontals per wall at 10 in maximum each way, 2 in clear cover, verticals 12 in into the cap. The vertical bar position is the left wall's (5.125 in from the recessed face), the less favourable of the two walls.
overview: Design of the two solid cheek walls on the ends of the pier cap, each 48 in high, 48 in wide (the full cap width) and 12 in thick, set 3 in in from the cap end, with a 30 by 30 in recessed panel 3/4 in deep and 9 in above the cap top on the outside face. Each wall is a vertical cantilever from the cap top. It retains no fill, carries no bearing and does not touch the superstructure, so wind acting directly on it is its only lateral load.

The wind pressure follows the superstructure wind calculation C001 and LRFD 3.8.1.2.1: the SDG Table 2.4.1-1 Strength III wind speed with the C001 exposure coefficient and gust factor, the Strength V and Service I speeds of LRFD Table 3.8.1.1.2-1 with K_Z = 1.0, and the substructure drag coefficient of LRFD Table 3.8.1.2.1-2, as for the direct pier wind of C002. Per LRFD 3.8.1.2.3b the pressure acts on the exposed face seen in elevation; the wall is designed for the full pressure normal to its broad face, which bounds the face component of every skewed wind direction, and the force on its 12 in edge is reported with the pier loads. The wind load factor of LRFD Table 3.4.1-1 is 1.0 in Strength III, Strength V and Service I. Wind on live load (LRFD 3.8.1.3), vertical wind (3.8.2) and aeroelastic effects (3.8.3) do not apply to a solid substructure wall on a pedestrian bridge.

The checks follow LRFD Section 5 for the reinforcement the CAD model carries: one centred mat of six #4 verticals and six #4 horizontals per wall at 10 in maximum each way, 2 in clear cover, verticals developed straight 12 in into the cap. Flexure and minimum reinforcement are checked at the cap top (section A, full thickness) and at the bottom of the recessed panel (section B, net thickness); crack control applies only where the service tension exceeds 0.8 fr; shear uses the simplified β; interface shear uses the SDG 1.15 clean-joint factors; the straight development of the verticals carries the confinement and excess reinforcement factors; shrinkage and temperature steel, bar spacing, cover and the minimum thickness complete the register.
outside: cap-end flexure and torsion from the wall moment, the cap stirrup and end-bar layout around the embedded verticals, the architectural panel and chamfer detailing, and the pier analysis model, which carries the direct wall wind as node loads.

t_B: The 3/4 in panel is taken off the full thickness over the panel height; the chamfer at its edge is ignored.
H_B: Wind above the panel bottom produces the moment at section B; the 9 in border below the panel is full thickness.
A_face: The broad face seen in elevation across the bridge. The cap top is the lower edge; nothing shields the wall.
A_edge: The 12 in edge seen along the bridge. Its force is a pier load; it bends the wall about its strong axis and is not a wall check.
z_c: Uniform pressure on a rectangular face: the resultant acts at mid-height.
W_wall: About 2.3 kip per wall. Its compression would raise the flexural and interface resistance slightly; it is left out.
q_III: LRFD Eq. 3.8.1.2.1-1 without the drag coefficient; the gust factor is already included. The C001 exposure coefficient is for the common 35.7 ft crown height and bounds the wall top.
P_III: The substructure drag coefficient 1.6 of LRFD Table 3.8.1.2.1-2, the same as the direct pier wind of C002.
P_str: Both strength combinations carry WS = 1.0 (LRFD Table 3.4.1-1), so the larger pressure, Strength III, is the design pressure.
P_ser: Service I with WS = 1.0: the pressure for crack control.
F_T_III: 0.96 kip per wall at Strength III, the +1.9 kip for both walls recorded in the 19 October load review of the pier analysis.
M_T_III: The wall's moment about the cap top. The cap end carries it in flexure and torsion, outside this calculation.
F_L_III: Wind along the bridge on the 12 in edge; 0.24 kip per wall.
F_T_III_both: Both walls together; compare with the pier node loads of the analysis model.
w_u: Pressure times the full 48 in width: the wall is designed as one 4 ft wide cantilever with its six verticals, not as a 1 ft strip.
V_u: The whole wind on the face arrives at the construction joint as shear.
M_u_A: Uniform load on a cantilever: w H² / 2 at the fixed end.
M_u_B: The same cantilever formula with the height above the panel bottom.
A_s: All six verticals cross the base and the panel section; wind from either side puts them in tension.
d_A: The mat sits 5.125 in from the recessed face on the left wall, so the verticals are nearer one face than the other; wind from the side that puts the far face in compression gives the smaller depth.
d_B: At the panel the recessed face is 3/4 in closer to the bar: compression on that face gives the smallest depth in the wall.
phi_A: Tension-controlled: the strain in the verticals is far above 0.005.
M_cr_A: The 48 in wide, 12 in thick gross section with the modulus of rupture and the LRFD 5.6.3.3 factors.
M_min_A: 1.33 Mu governs: the wind moment is far below the cracking moment, so the mat need not reach Mcr.
A_req_A: The steel 1.33 Mu requires, the basis of the excess reinforcement factor in the development check.
f_ct_A: Compared with 0.8 fr: when below it the section is uncracked at Service I and LRFD 5.6.7 does not apply.
s_cr_A: 99 in records that the crack-control spacing limit does not apply; the spacing checks fall back to LRFD 5.10.3.2 and 5.10.6.
d_v_A: 0.72 h governs for the thin wall.
V_c_A: Simplified LRFD 5.7.3.4.1 with β = 2.0: the wall has no transverse reinforcement and is less than 16 in thick.
lambda_rc: db / cb with cb the cover to the bar centre in the cap (3.25 in at the outer verticals), not less than 0.4; transverse reinforcement is not credited.
lambda_er: The wind demand is small, so the excess reinforcement credit is large; LRFD 5.10.8.2.1a still requires 12 in.
l_d_full: What a straight bar needs to develop fy without the excess reinforcement credit: about 12.3 in, just above the 12 in embedment.
l_d: With the excess reinforcement credit the 12 in floor governs, which the 12 in embedment meets exactly.
V_ni: Clean joint not intentionally roughened (SDG 1.15): c = 0.075 ksi, μ = 0.6; the cohesion and the clamping of the six verticals both count.
A_vf_min: 0.05 Acv / fy; the six verticals provide more than twice this.
A_ts_mat: LRFD 5.10.6 distributes the steel to both faces; with one centred mat the sum of both face requirements is applied, the convention of the end-bent cheek walls.
A_pr_v: Six verticals over the 48 in width: 0.30 in²/ft.
A_pr_h: Six horizontals over the 48 in height: 0.30 in²/ft.
s_clr_prov: The two outer verticals are 3 in apart (2.5 in clear) and the two top horizontals 3.5 in apart (3 in clear).
DC_develop: 1.00: the 12 in embedment equals the 12 in minimum; without the excess reinforcement credit the straight length would be 12.3 in.

working_notes: Starting case: the pier cheek walls and mats of the current CAD model (decisions D-059 and D-061; model evidence 2026-10-19-pier-cheek-relief and 2026-10-19-pier-cheek-development). The vertical bar position x_v is the left wall's 5.125 in from the recessed face (the right wall's mat is centred, 5.75 in); the governing wall is used for both. Wind inputs V_III, V_V, V_SI, K_Z_gov and G_fac are the journal values of C001. The calculation number C018 is proposed; the calculation is not yet a journal module.

single_mat.text: One centred mat accepted in place of the two-face distribution of LRFD 5.10.6 for the 12 in walls (the end-bent cheek walls follow the same convention, decision D-039).
